reason: profiles/pi began as pi-sandbox-guard 7ad441f's Pi profile and is maintained in this repository (docs/DESIGN.md section 15, decision D17). The differences are the changes Agent Guard made to it, numbered as code comments cite them. test/pi-launch.mjs tests differences 1 to 5, 7, 9, 13 and 18, test/pi-commands.sh difference 6 and profiles/pi/test/checker.mjs difference 17.

differences.change: Agent Guard's base write protections, appended after pi-sandbox-guard's rules: the engine folder, OpenCode Guard's engine folder, ~/Agent Guard, ~/Applications/Agent Guard.app, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.opencode, ~/.cc-safety-net except its logs, ~/Library/LaunchAgents and the eight shell startup files, plus the resolved target of each one that is a symlink at launch (engine/launch's rule: it exists and resolves elsewhere), passed as AG_LINK_* parameters with an inert path when there is no link. For ~/.config/opencode alone, a missing final directory also resolves through its parent, so linked ancestors cannot leave first-launch config and plugins writable. Every folder above a resolved target, up to and not including /, is pinned with a literal deny, as engine/launch pins them, through 32 fixed AG_PIN_* slots, shared with difference 4's cache roots (unused slots inert); a launch that needs more slots is refused. Fixed slots keep the profile one static file passed with -f, with the paths as parameters rather than generated SBPL text.

A project that is, contains or is inside one of difference 1's folders is refused before launch, beside the preamble's existing boundary and agent-config refusals; all of ~/.cc-safety-net is refused, its logs included. For a folder that is a symlink, a project that is or is inside its resolved target is refused too, since the session would be wholly read-only; a project that only contains the target launches with the target write-denied, as for the shell startup files, whose targets are never refused.

Decision D7, as in engine/profile.sb: (deny lsopen), (deny job-creation) and (deny process-exec) of /usr/bin/open, /usr/bin/osascript, /usr/bin/osacompile, /usr/bin/codesign, /usr/sbin/diskutil, /bin/launchctl and /usr/bin/sudo.

Step 7's protections under Pi's ~/.cache grant, for C = ~/.cache as written, C = its canonical path (AG_CACHE_HOME, resolved after the folders below are created, since Seatbelt checks resolved paths and ~/.cache may be a link) and C = the canonical XDG_CACHE_HOME: writes to C/opencode/packages, C/opencode/node_modules, OpenCode's legacy install metadata C/opencode/package.json, C/opencode/package-lock.json and C/opencode/bun.lock, C/opencode/bin, C/opencode/models.json (each as a subpath) and C/opencode/models-*.json are denied, and C and C/opencode are pinned with literal denies. Every folder above each C, up to and not including /, is pinned through difference 1's AG_PIN_* slots, so no cache root can be moved away by renaming a folder above it, such as the parent of an XDG_CACHE_HOME inside the project. XDG_CACHE_HOME travels as AG_XDG_CACHE_HOME, ~/.cache when unset; a value that is not an existing absolute folder refuses the launch. Before sandbox-exec the preamble creates C/opencode/bin at both roots (mkdir -p, so also C and C/opencode on a fresh account), because OpenCode creates a missing bin at every start and the profile denies that create (docs/DESIGN.md section 9).

User-facing repair text names Agent Guard's commands instead of pi-sandbox-guard's npm commands, which no longer exist after the adoption: the preamble's messages and its binding comment say agent-guard bind instead of npm run bind and drop 'from the repo checkout'; src/index.mjs's FILTER-ONLY warning says to install Agent Guard (agent-guard update, or the one-line installer) and run agent-guard bind instead of npm run deploy:launchers and npm run bind from a checkout; launchers/example-custom's installation instruction says agent-guard wrapper add instead of scripts/deploy-launchers.sh --extra-launchers; its missing-shim message says to install Agent Guard first (agent-guard update, or the one-line installer) instead of npm run deploy:launchers.

scripts/bind-executable.sh runs as agent-guard bind (commands/bind.zsh) instead of npm run bind: its usage, hints and executables.conf header name agent-guard bind; every mode but --show stops when node is not on PATH, which npm run guaranteed; --checker-node [PATH], which recorded the analyzer's Node in the extension's .guard-node, is accepted and ignored with one line on stderr, and alone it does nothing; an executables.conf that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is refused before it is written; Pi and OMP bind independently, so a Mac with only OMP records omp= alone, and a recorded pi=, omp= or node= that no longer validates is dropped (node= is detected again) with a note instead of stopping the command; an empty candidate list no longer fails under bash 3.2.

Step 7f (docs/DESIGN.md section 12): the project agent config deny write-denies all of .opencode instead of .opencode/plugins, OpenCode's config file names (opencode.json, opencode.jsonc, tui.json, tui.jsonc) and .cc-safety-net, anywhere under the project. Without it a Pi session could plant an OpenCode plugin or config that a later OpenCode session in the project loads, or a .cc-safety-net/policy.json that switches off cc-safety-net's built-in rules there. The preamble's PROJECT refusal patterns, kept in step with the folder rules, refuse a project inside .opencode or .cc-safety-net; the file-name rules match only the file itself and need no refusal. Seatbelt checks the resolved path, so the preamble's symlinked-config check also refuses a launch where one of these names in the project or launch folder is a link whose target the session can write, or where a link inside .opencode or .cc-safety-net resolves to a writable place outside it, as it refuses a symlinked .pi or .omp; a link to a place the session cannot write, or to a project path whose own name the profile denies, launches, and one whose target is missing is refused, at the name or inside .opencode or .cc-safety-net.

Literal write denies pin PI_AGENT_STATE, OMP_AGENT_STATE, OMP_STATE_ROOT, OMP_BASE_ROOT and OMP_BASE_ROOT/profiles after every allow. The profiles pin prevents moving a named OMP profile through its writable ancestor; identical base/state paths share the same protection. Config denies stay attached to their paths while runtime descendants remain writable. The preamble creates only the active runtime's roots before confinement and refuses on failure, because the pins also deny creating those nodes inside the sandbox.
Load the release peer runtime grants before configuration denies and prepend session-only peer wrappers after PATH sanitization. Preserve the original PATH for peer discovery.

When Git selects the project boundary, require it to match the physical checkout root found through the nearest .git directory or file. A session-writable core.worktree cannot redirect the next launch to a sibling or ancestor. Explicit PI_PROJECT retains operator-selected boundaries; linked worktrees and non-Git folders remain supported.

Write-deny mcp.json at the active Pi state root, as models.json is. Pi loads that file's MCP servers at every session start and runs each stdio server's command; OMP's mcp.json and .mcp.json were already denied. Pi's /mcp manager cannot save server changes from a guarded session.

Write-deny bin and tools at the active Pi state root. Pi 1.3.0 puts bin first on every Bash command's PATH and prefers its rg and fd, and moves tools/fd and tools/rg into bin at startup, so a planted file there would run in later sessions. A guarded session cannot download a missing rg or fd; Pi warns and continues. The preamble creates bin before confinement with the Pi state root, because Pi's startup migration of a legacy tools/rg or tools/fd stops Pi when it cannot create a missing bin.

Permit the directory node of project .pi/settings.json.lock so Pi can acquire its directory lock when reading settings. Regular files, symlinks, lock contents, other configuration locks and paths outside PROJECT receive no grant. Settings and surrounding configuration remain protected.

Deny connections to the agents that hold keys, unless the operator sets AGENT_GUARD_SSH_AGENT=allow outside the guard: ssh-agent's launchd socket under /private/var/run or /private/tmp, and sockets under ~/.ssh and ~/.gnupg, where gpg-agent and SSH control sockets live. Sessions already run without SSH_AUTH_SOCK and cannot read those folders, but a file deny does not stop a socket connection, so the agents could be used with every loaded key (docs/DESIGN.md decision D15). Other Unix sockets stay reachable.

The extension checks tool calls with cc-safety-net's Pi entry from the release (vendor/cc-safety-net/dist/pi/index.js), through a stand-in Pi API that captures its tool_call handler, for shell tools only (bash and powershell; file tools and other tools pass), once for each candidate working folder with the worst result kept, in place of the analyzer, whose files (src/guard-core.mjs, src/validate-bash-command.sh) and suites (test/smoke.mjs, test/corpus.mjs, test/corpus/corpus.json) are no longer in the profile, with the analyzer's differences 8 and 15. The verdicts are allow or block: there are no confirmations. The policy is the session copy of the user's cc-safety-net configuration under decision D13 (docs/DESIGN.md section 5, Command checker), which the preamble builds at launch, outside the sandbox, with the release's checker/snapshot.zsh into <engine>/state/pi/<release>.XXXXXXXX/checker, a folder the profile write-protects with the engine folder; the preamble exports CC_SAFETY_NET_HOME, AGENT_GUARD_RELEASE, CC_SAFETY_NET_PROJECT_TIGHTEN_ONLY=1 and the level (standard unless CC_SAFETY_NET_LEVEL=paranoid), clears the other CC_SAFETY_NET_* selectors, and removes, in the background, session folders from before the last boot. The extension blocks every tool call, naming the repair, when the session copy is missing or outside that state folder, cc-safety-net fails to load, or the probe `git config core.hooksPath agent-guard-probe` is not denied by Agent Guard's hooks-path rule; it also blocks when the copy's rule.json or Agent Guard's rulebook disappears later. The FILTER-ONLY diagnostic and the per-event de-duplication stay. A Pi started without the shim has no session copy, so its extension blocks every call.

The launcher no longer reads the extension folder's .guard-node, which recorded the Node that ran the analyzer, and no longer refuses to launch when it is invalid, stale or inside a sandbox-writable root. The analyzer is retired (difference 17), so a leftover .guard-node, which Agent Guard's update and uninstall remove, has no effect; this also ends the defect that a Pi started inside a Pi session exited with HOME_CANON: parameter not set whenever .guard-node existed.

Check for newer stable Agent Guard releases once before a top-level Pi or OMP session, after account and nesting resolution. Runtime administrative commands and help/version requests do not check. Accepted upgrades use the existing updater and exec the installed shim once with the original arguments; an internal handoff marker skips only the repeated update check.

Code with no caller in Agent Guard is removed: from scripts/lib-ops.sh, the helpers of pi-sandbox-guard's deploy, status and hook scripts (ops_die, ops_say, ops_warn, ops_require_single_line, ops_hash_file, ops_require_same_hash, ops_git_meta, ops_make_release_id, ops_stamp_get, ops_json_quote, ops_default_guard_dest, ops_default_launchers_dest), keeping ops_stable_node_path and ops_path_is_known_sandbox_write_root, which bind-executable.sh and installer/harness/pi.zsh call; from scripts/check-launchers.mjs, the --deployed mode and its PI_SANDBOX_CHECK_DEPLOYED and PI_SANDBOX_DEPLOYED_ROOT variables, which checked pi-sandbox-guard's deployed launchers in ~/.local/bin and which Agent Guard never ran (docs/DESIGN.md section 11).

Comments in the preamble name the block of engine/launch that implements the same launch policy (account home, Git selectors and checkout check, project refusals, active hooks folder, protected link targets and pins, peer runtime, checker level, SSH agent switch), so a fix to one is made to both; engine/launch carries the matching comments. No behavior change.

test_notes: test/pi.sh runs profiles/pi/test/shim.mjs with the recorded edit: its launch cases run the preamble against the account's real home, because its fixtures keep the real directory-service lookup. Since difference 4 they create ~/.cache/opencode/bin in that account when it is missing, as they already create and remove ~/.local/share/pi-sandbox-bindable-* folders. Difference 9 also prepares active Pi/OMP roots there, including ~/.omp/agent, ~/.omp/profiles and named profiles; run these cases in a disposable account.

test_edits.change: sb, sb_omp and sb_pi_relocated pass the profile's AG_* parameters with inert values (the cache roots as HOME/.cache), read from the profile, since a missing parameter stops the profile from compiling. The relocated Pi fixture creates its root before confinement, as the launcher does, so the root pin does not deny first-launch runtime setup. check_user_state_protection also checks mcp.json, bin and tools at each Pi and OMP state root.
The launcher check no longer requires executable_under_sandbox_write_root, which the launcher used only to validate the guard Node binding.

runNestedShim passes the profile's AG_* parameters with inert values (the cache roots as HOME/.cache), read from the profile; the ambient-override refusal case expects agent-guard bind instead of npm run bind; the case that a .guard-node inside PROJECT refuses the launch now expects the launch to succeed.
